annotations.label: First isomorphism theorem (groups)
annotations.note: Verified: `QuotientGroup.quotientKerEquivRange` gives `G ⧸ ker φ ≃* range φ` for a group homomorphism.

annotations.label: Second isomorphism theorem (groups)
annotations.note: Verified: `QuotientGroup.quotientInfEquivProdNormalQuotient` states `H/(H ∩ N) ≃* HN/N` for `N` normal.

annotations.label: Projective linear group via second isomorphism theorem

anchor.snippet: An application of the second isomorphism theorem identifies projective linear groups

annotations.note: Mathlib defines `Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup` as `GL n R ⧸ Subgroup.center (GL n R)` directly, without deriving it as an instance of the second isomorphism theorem.

annotations.label: Third isomorphism theorem and correspondence (groups)
annotations.note: Verified: `QuotientGroup.quotientQuotientEquivQuotient` gives `(G/N)/(M/N) ≃* G/M` when `N ≤ M`.

annotations.label: Correspondence/lattice theorem (groups)
annotations.note: Verified: `QuotientGroup.comapMk'OrderIso` is the order isomorphism between subgroups of `G ⧸ N` and subgroups of `G` containing `N`.

annotations.label: Splitting lemma

anchor.snippet: left splits and right splits are equivalent by the splitting lemma

annotations.note: Mathlib provides `CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.Splitting` in abelian categories, encoding the classical left/right split equivalence through the general splitting API rather than as a single named lemma.

annotations.label: Nine lemma

anchor.snippet: The third isomorphism theorem is generalized by the nine lemma to abelian categories

annotations.note: Mathlib has snake- and four-lemma infrastructure in `CategoryTheory.Abelian.DiagramLemmas` but no explicit 3×3 (nine) lemma statement.

annotations.label: First isomorphism theorem (rings)
annotations.note: Verified: `RingHom.quotientKerEquivRange` gives `R ⧸ ker f ≃+* f.range` for a ring homomorphism.

annotations.label: Second isomorphism theorem (rings)
annotations.note: Verified: `RingCon.comapQuotientEquivRange` phrases the second isomorphism theorem for rings via ring congruences, generalizing the classical `(S+I)/I ≅ S/(S∩I)`.

annotations.label: First isomorphism theorem (modules)
annotations.note: Verified: `LinearMap.quotKerEquivRange` provides `M ⧸ ker f ≃ₗ[R] range f` for a linear map `f`.

annotations.label: Second isomorphism theorem (modules)
annotations.note: Verified: `LinearMap.quotientInfEquivSupQuotient` gives `p ⧸ (p ⊓ p') ≃ₗ (p ⊔ p') ⧸ p'`.

annotations.note: Verified: `Submodule.quotientQuotientEquivQuotient` gives `(M/S)/(T/S) ≃ₗ[R] M/T` when `S ≤ T`.

annotations.label: Congruence on an algebra
annotations.note: Mathlib has structure-specific congruences (`Con`, `AddCon`, `RingCon`) and `Setoid`, but no general universal-algebra congruence framework.

annotations.label: First isomorphism theorem (universal algebra)
annotations.note: Verified: `Con.quotientKerEquivRange` and analogues (`RingCon`, `Setoid`) exist, but Mathlib has no universal-algebra-level statement.

annotations.label: Second isomorphism theorem (universal algebra)
annotations.note: Only structure-specific versions (`Con.comapQuotientEquiv`, `RingCon.comapQuotientEquivRange`, `LinearMap.quotientInfEquivSupQuotient`) are formalized.

annotations.label: Third isomorphism theorem (universal algebra)
annotations.note: Verified: `Setoid.quotientQuotientEquivQuotient` plus `Con`/`RingCon` variants exist, but no universal-algebra statement.
